exemplars.answer: Let the three consecutive integers be n, n + 1 and n + 2. Their sum is n + (n + 1) + (n + 2) = 3n + 3 = 3(n + 1). Since n + 1 is an integer, 3(n + 1) is a multiple of 3, so the sum of any three consecutive integers is a multiple of 3.
Call the numbers n, n + 1 and n + 2. Adding them gives n + n + 1 + n + 2 = 3n + 3.
The numbers are n, n + 1 and n + 2. Adding them: n + n + 1 + n + 2 = 3n + 2.
